transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m having trouble keeping my mind on one thing at work. I’ll be doing an inventory count, then a beeper goes off or a forklift alarm sounds, or somebody moves a pallet, and I get pulled away from it. Then I look back and realize I entered the wrong numbers.
Do you remember having similar trouble staying focused or being easily distracted back when you were a child or in school?

No, I don’t really remember it being like this when I was younger. It’s more lately—at work, any little noise or movement pulls me off what I’m counting, and then I find I’ve entered the wrong numbers.
Did these concentration problems start around the same time as any particular stressful event or major change in your life, like a new job, relationship issue, or loss?
It’s been about a month. My husband stopped working outside the home, so our usual routine changed around then.
Besides trouble concentrating at work, have you noticed yourself worrying a lot or feeling anxious about various things in your daily life lately?
I haven’t really noticed a lot of worrying about different things. It’s mostly just the trouble focusing at work.
Since your husband stopped working and this started, have you been feeling down, sad, or less interested in things you normally enjoy?
I haven’t really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things. It’s mainly been the focus problem at work.
Do you notice this same trouble concentrating in other situations outside of work, such as at home or when reading or having conversations?

Mostly at work. I’ll be doing an inventory count, and a beeper or forklift alarm—or somebody moving a pallet—pulls my attention right off it. Then I look back and realize I’ve entered the wrong numbers.
Aside from getting distracted by noises, have you noticed any other changes, like forgetting things you normally remember or having trouble finding the right words?
No, I haven’t noticed forgetting things or having trouble finding words. It’s really just that I get thrown off when there’s noise at work.
How have you been feeling emotionally about the change in your routine since your husband stopped working outside the home—does it cause you stress or unease?
I’m not really sure it’s caused me much stress or unease. I mean, the routine is different, but I haven’t noticed feeling particularly upset about it.
Since your husband's schedule changed, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?
I haven’t really noticed any change in my sleep since then.

Does the trouble concentrating happen specifically when there's a sudden noise or movement around you, or do you also find your mind wandering even when the environment is quiet and there's nothing obvious pulling your attention away?

Mostly when something around me pulls my attention. At the warehouse, a beeper or forklift alarm, or somebody moving a pallet, throws me off what I’m counting. Then I’ll realize I put the wrong numbers into the inventory.
Have you started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medications, supplements, caffeine, alcohol, or other substances around the time this started a month ago?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any change like that around when this started.
